summary: Math is MATH 19, 20 and 21 plus CME 100 or both MATH 51 and 52; science and engineering fundamentals are the listed courses; the depth is the eleven CHEMENG courses (CHEMENG 100 and 105 still count for students who took them before 2026-27). CHEMENG 185A is also your WIM course and CHEMENG 185B your capstone; no other course counts twice. Every course must be letter graded if the instructor offers a letter grade, and the audit counts 95 units. You check by hand your Technology in Society course from the School of Engineering list and the 2.0 combined GPA in engineering fundamentals and depth. Honors needs three letter-graded quarters of CHEMENG 190H (9 units) and 3 units of CHEMENG 191H, and you check by hand the 3.5 GPA, the poster presentation and the thesis.

program.why: Grading: "All courses taken for the major must be taken for a letter grade if the instructor offers that option." Policies: "A course may only be counted towards one requirement, not double-counted." The WIM and capstone blocks still share, because the depth text says "CHEMENG 185A will also satisfy the Writing in the Major (WiM) requirement, and CHEMENG 185B will also satisfy the Capstone requirement."
